newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian most liquid shares firm, seen firming.
newsitem.headline: Russian most liquid shares firm, seen firming.

text.p: Leading Russian shares reflected a glimmer of interest unusual over the last couple of weeks' trade, dealers said on Wednesday, predicting the most liquid shares might lead second-tier stocks at the end of the week.

"At the end of the day there was some interest in blue chips. If you have large amounts of money in the market, you have to go into them," said Brunswick's Martin Diggle who said LUKoil and Irkutskenergo had both seen interest.
He saw the market firming through the week, led by the best known shares.
The Russian Trading System 24-share Index firmed about half a percent to 192.03 from 190.88 on $16.9 million trade in the market.
Irkutskenergo closed Wednesday at $0.120 after $0.124 the day earlier, LUKoil firmed to $10.70 from $10.61.
Noyabrskneftegaz ordinaries rose to $5.95 from $5.52 and prefs to $3.85 from $3.65.
"The general feeling is that demand for the illiquids has slackened a bit. More importantly, clients are stopping buying," said Pavel Gronbjerg of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Gavin Rankin, chief researcher at Troika-Dialog, said investors were unlikely in large numbers to leave utilities (also known as energos), telecoms and oil companies for other, unexplored sectors.
"Those things make up the majority indexes. And investors are focused towards liquidity and indexes," he said.
"It is considerably easier to explain another energo to an investor than how an engineering company works," he added, saying that the interest in the companies was often justified.
Traders said Irkutskenergo was hurt by Tuesday's late announcement of a $13.7 million pre-tax loss, but was still attracting interest because of its plans to issue ADRs.
